basic_identification.full_title: Geosynthetics — Guidelines for Installation of Geotexiles as Pavement Fabric
basic_identification.sector_category: Technical Textiles / Geosynthetics (approved by the Textile Division Council and finalized by the Geosynthetics Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard prescribes guidelines for the installation of geotextiles as pavement fabric (paving fabric) inside road pavements to provide waterproofing, stress relief, and barrier separation, thereby retarding reflective cracking in asphalt concrete overlays.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Installation Guideline (Geosynthetics / Civil Engineering Infrastructure)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Statutory Voluntary Guideline for Installation, but under the mandatory 'Geotextiles (Quality Control) Order' (issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India), the geotextile/geosynthetic materials (pavement fabrics) themselves must conform to Indian Standards and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Laying pavement fabrics without certified materials is a punishable statutory offense. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic polymer paving fabrics.

requirements.detail: During installation, the paving fabric must be rolled out such that the fuzzy (heat-bonded or non-woven lofted) side of the paving fabric is laid down directly into the hot asphalt tack coat, leaving the smooth side facing up.
The tack coat application rate must be sufficient to saturate the geotextile fabric and form a waterproof bond with the existing pavement surface. Solvents and cutbacks must not be used.

Cationic and anionic asphalt emulsions may be used successfully, provided: a) The paving fabric is laid only after allowing the specified time for curing (break) of the emulsion; b) No traffic is allowed over the area where the tack coat is applied; and c) They are applied at a higher rate to compensate for the water content.

requirements.requirement_type: Traffic Braking and Intersection Rate Reduction
requirements.detail: In zones of heavy vehicle braking—including street intersections, steep grades, and deceleration lanes—the normal tack coat application rate must be reduced by approximately 20 percent as directed by the engineer to prevent fabric slippage or fatting-up of asphalt.

When encountering drains, manholes, joints, or other road irregularities, the geotextile must be placed normally and then cut cleanly around the obstruction. Any wrinkles exceeding 25 mm must be slit open and flatly overlapped.

Prior to applying the asphalt concrete (AC) overlay, the laid geotextile must be formally inspected by a certified inspector of the engineer to verify that the fabric has suffered zero installation damage. Damaged geotextile must be immediately repaired or replaced.

The geotextile must be utilized to rehabilitate localized distressed areas, utility cuts, and excessively cracked pavement prior to an AC overlay, using either a full-width layer or targeted membrane strips depending on distress severity.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16343 : 2015 is the national Indian Standard code of practice specifying guidelines for the correct field installation of geotextile paving fabrics (pavement fabrics) inside road pavements to retard reflective cracking in asphalt overlays. While the installation process is a guideline, the synthetic polymer geotextile materials used must conform to Indian Standards and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under statutory Quality Control Orders. The standard outlines strict procedural controls—including spraying a uniform hot asphalt tack coat (excluding cutbacks and solvent-laden emulsions), laying the paving fabric with its fuzzy side down into the tack coat (leaving the smooth side up) to ensure deep saturation and waterproof bonding, reducing tack coat rates by 20% in high-braking zones and street intersections to avoid fabric sliding, slitting and overlapping any structural wrinkles exceeding 25 mm, and enforcing a mandatory pre-covering inspection by a certified inspector to verify that the fabric has suffered zero tears or installation damage before the final asphalt concrete overlay is placed.
